input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Validate GPU usage metering data schema for chargeback reporting

## Description

The GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) is in flight and owns the
per-project GPU-hour usage data schema, which is not final until that strategy
lands. This investigation resolves the strategy's open question — the external
timing and shape of that schema — by tracking it as it stabilizes and
validating that it can support administrator chargeback reporting. It produces
the reporting-side data contract that the reporting implementation builds
against: which fields are consumed, the per-project aggregation rules, and how
reporting accesses the metering data.

## Scope

- Map the finalized (or latest draft) metering data schema field-by-field
  against the reporting needs: per-project GPU-hour totals, selectable time
  ranges, and current-month windows.
- Identify gaps where the schema cannot support reporting (project
  attribution, time granularity, GPU-hour definition) and raise them to the
  metering strategy owners, with each gap's disposition recorded.
- Define the reporting-side data contract: consumed fields, per-project
  aggregation rules, and the access path by which reporting reads the metering
  data.
- Record the agreed contract as the deliverable that downstream reporting work
  builds against, including a go/no-go conclusion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written schema-to-reporting mapping exists covering every field the
  reporting needs (project identity, GPU-hours, timestamps), with each need
  marked supported or gap.
- Every gap has a recorded disposition: accepted limitation, or extension
  request formally raised to the metering strategy owners.
- The reporting data contract (consumed fields, aggregation rules, access
  path) is documented and confirmed with the metering data owners.
- A go/no-go conclusion is recorded: the finalized schema either supports
  per-project GPU-hour reporting over selectable time ranges, or the required
  extensions have been formally requested.

## HLR Traceability

- Enables HLR-1, HLR-2, and HLR-3 by resolving the strategy's open question on
  metering data schema finalization; this investigation does not itself
  implement any HLR.

## Risks / Notes

- External timing risk: the schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands.
  The investigation can start against drafts but cannot conclude before
  finalization; the timing is outside this strategy's control.
- The Dashboard owns no data plane (Kubernetes API only per architecture
  context), so the contract must also settle how reporting accesses
  time-series metering data, not just its schema.

# Per-project Kueue quota reference and GPU-hour attribution semantics

## Description

Delivers the Distributed Workloads side of the chargeback reporting
capability: a validated per-project Kueue quota reference (per-project quota
totals derived from the platform's ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model) and
the agreed GPU-hour attribution semantics — what counts as a GPU-hour relative
to Kueue quota admission and usage. The quota reference is delivered as a
machine-readable runtime artifact — per-project quota totals exported as
versioned Prometheus metrics from the Distributed Workloads side, extending
the existing Kueue-metrics-to-Prometheus pattern — and the attribution
semantics as a versioned written definition in the owning repository; the
administrator reporting view and the report documentation build on both. The
component itself keeps working with no
collection changes; the metering pipeline is out of scope (RHAISTRAT-9990).

## Scope

- Define and validate the mapping from the Kueue quota model
  (ClusterQueue/LocalQueue) to per-project quota totals, covering every
  project that holds quota.
- Define the GPU-hour attribution semantics for chargeback reporting: how
  consumed GPU-hours are attributed to projects relative to quota admission
  and usage, i.e. what counts as a GPU-hour for reporting purposes.
- Validate both the quota mapping and the attribution semantics against
  representative quota configurations.
- Deliver the validated quota reference as a machine-readable runtime
  artifact: per-project quota totals exposed as versioned Prometheus metrics
  (documented metric names and labels) from the Distributed Workloads side,
  extending the existing Kueue-metrics-to-Prometheus pattern, so the Dashboard
  reporting view consumes them programmatically rather than re-deriving quota
  from CRs.
- Deliver the attribution semantics as a versioned written definition in the
  owning repository that the report documentation incorporates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-project quota totals can be derived for every project holding a
  LocalQueue, with the derivation rules documented.
- The GPU-hour attribution semantics are documented and validated against
  representative quota configurations.
- Per-project quota totals are exposed as versioned Prometheus metrics with
  documented metric names and labels, queryable for every project holding a
  LocalQueue — a runtime artifact the Dashboard reporting view consumes
  programmatically, not a prose-only specification.
- The GPU-hour attribution semantics are recorded as a versioned written
  definition in the owning repository.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, quota side): provides the per-project Kueue quota reference that
  current-month consumption is compared against.
- Grounds the report semantics documented under HLR-4 (what counts as a
  GPU-hour).

## Notes

- This is a validation deliverable owned by the Distributed Workloads team as
  the owner of the Kueue quota model; it involves no metering collection work
  (owned by RHAISTRAT-9990) and no currency/cost-rate modelling (out of scope).

# Administrator GPU chargeback reporting in the Dashboard

## Description

The administrator-facing chargeback reporting capability in the Dashboard:
per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges computed
from the metering data delivered by the GPU usage metering strategy, a
current-month admin view showing consumption against each project's Kueue
quota, CSV export of reports, and a stable API for finance tooling. This epic
consumes metering data; it must not re-implement collection.

## Scope

- Administrator report view: per-project GPU-hour consumption over selectable
  time ranges, computed from the metering data per the agreed reporting data
  contract (project attribution and aggregation rules).
- Current-month admin view showing each project's consumption against its
  Kueue quota, using the validated per-project quota reference and GPU-hour
  attribution semantics.
- CSV export of reports.
- Stable API exposing report data for retrieval by finance tooling.
- Administrator-only visibility of the chargeback reporting views, consistent
  with platform RBAC.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over
  selectable time ranges.
- The admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue
  quota.
- Reports can be exported as CSV.
- Report data is retrievable via a stable API usable by finance tooling.
- The chargeback reporting views are visible only to administrators, per
  platform RBAC.
- Report values are computed from the metering data per the agreed reporting
  data contract — no collection logic is re-implemented in the Dashboard.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges.
- HLR-2 (P1, bundled with HLR-1): CSV export and stable API are retrieval
  modes of the same report surface and data.
- HLR-3 (P1, view side): current-month consumption against each project's
  Kueue quota in the Dashboard admin view.

## Risks / Notes

- External timing risk: this work is gated on the finalized metering data
  schema from the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990); if
  the finalized schema does not support the reporting needs, the
  implementation is rewritten against the actual schema shape (or extensions
  are requested to the metering strategy) before proceeding.

# Chargeback report semantics and export integration documentation

## Description

Documentation for the GPU chargeback reporting capability, covering report
semantics — what counts as a GPU-hour and how consumption is attributed to
projects against their Kueue quota — and export integration for finance
tooling via CSV export and the stable report API.

## Scope

- Report semantics documentation topic:
  - What counts as a GPU-hour for chargeback reporting, per the agreed
    attribution semantics derived from the Kueue quota model.
  - How per-project consumption is attributed and what the comparison against
    each project's Kueue quota means.
- Export integration documentation topic:
  - How to export reports as CSV.
  - How finance tooling retrieves report data via the stable report API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) consistent
  with the agreed attribution semantics and the implemented reporting.
- Documentation covers export integration (CSV export and stable API usage)
  for finance tooling.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented chargeback
  reporting capability.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9018 (GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators)

Strategy status: Refinement Done, priority Major. The strategy builds
administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of per-project GPU-hour
metering data delivered by the in-flight RHAISTRAT-9990 strategy, whose data
schema is not final until that strategy lands.

## Step 0 Triage

Not triaged. The strategy is not below threshold: it affects two components
(Dashboard, Distributed Workloads), and its single open question — the
finalization of the metering data schema owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 — is a
genuine unknown whose answer changes what the reporting implementation builds
against. It is not documentation-only: HLR-1 through HLR-3 require code work.
Full decomposition (Steps 1-8) was executed.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E001 | Validate GPU usage metering data schema for chargeback reporting | Investigation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E002 | Per-project Kueue quota reference and GPU-hour attribution semantics | Implementation | Distributed Workloads | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 | Administrator GPU chargeback reporting in the Dashboard | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9018-E004 | Chargeback report semantics and export integration documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |

Priorities: E001 is P0 because it gates the P0 reporting implementation
(HLR-1). E003 is P0 via HLR-1. E002 inherits P0 by priority inheritance: the
reporting epic builds against its quota/semantics contract and transitively
enables HLR-1, even though E002's only direct HLR (HLR-3) is P1 — see Health
Warnings. E004 is a `docs-authoring` epic exempt from priority inheritance;
its P1 derives from the strategy frontmatter priority `Major` (Major → P1).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Investigation: metering schema contract"] --> E003["E003 Dashboard chargeback reporting"]
    E002["E002 Quota reference + attribution semantics"] --> E003
    E002 --> E004["E004 Documentation"]
    E003 --> E004
```

Roots (no dependencies): E001, E002. Critical path: E001 → E003 → E004
(length 3).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E003 | Rule 3 (Investigation gates downstream) | The strategy's open question — the metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands — determines what the reporting implementation builds against. The investigation produces the reporting-side data contract; until it resolves, the reporting epic's approach is unknown. True gate: `rewrite` — if the finalized schema does not support per-project GPU-hour aggregation, the reporting implementation is rewritten against the actual schema (or extensions are requested to the metering strategy). |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact another epic builds against) | E002 delivers the validated per-project Kueue quota reference as a runtime artifact — per-project quota totals exported as versioned Prometheus metrics, extending the existing Kueue-metrics-to-Prometheus pattern — plus the GPU-hour attribution semantics as a versioned written definition; the Dashboard reporting view's code builds against that data shape to render consumption-vs-quota comparison. Not a configuration reference — the quota mapping and semantics define the data shape the view consumes. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | The documentation epic must be blocked by every Implementation epic; it also derives its report-semantics content from the attribution semantics E002 defines. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation describes what was built — the reporting view, export, and API — so it lands last. |

No edges between E001 and E002: the quota-side work is independent of the
metering schema (the Kueue quota model is GA in-platform per architecture
context), so both roots run in parallel — this is the Tier 1 / Tier 2 split
below.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 | Core reporting view: per-project GPU-hour reports over selectable time ranges computed from metering data. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 | **Bundled** with HLR-1: CSV export and the stable API are presentation/retrieval modes of the same report data structure and API surface as HLR-1's reports. Splitting would create two epics building the same surface plus an artificial serialization edge between them; the P1 label reads as relative value, not a deferral signal. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9018-E002, RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 | Spans two components: E002 delivers the per-project quota reference and attribution semantics (Distributed Workloads side — separately schedulable, its own epic); E003 renders current-month consumption against quota in the admin view (Dashboard side). **Bundled** (Dashboard-side increment, P1 HLR in P0 epic E003): the current-month-vs-quota view is a presentation mode of the same administrator report surface and report data structure as HLR-1's P0 reports — E003 builds that surface once, so splitting the quota-comparison view into a separate epic would build the same admin surface twice and add an artificial serialization edge between the halves. The P1 label reads as relative value, not a deferral signal; the increment ships with the P0 reporting view. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9018-E004 | Documentation of report semantics and export integration; `docs-authoring` epic blocked by all Implementations. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing strategy sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no Impacted
   Teams table, no Dependencies table (only a frontmatter `depends-on` link),
   no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no non-functional requirements.
   Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the HLRs; owner teams were
   inferred from the architecture-context files (RHOAI Dashboard owns
   Dashboard; Distributed Workloads owns Distributed Workloads). The
   documentation epic's team is assumed to be RHOAI Dashboard (feature owner)
   because the strategy names no documentation owner — verify before submit.
2. **External timing risk** (the strategy's open question): the metering data
   schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands. This is outside this
   strategy's control; E001 converts it into a tracked gate with a `rewrite`
   failure impact, and Tier 2 work (E003, E004) is gated behind it.
3. **Priority inheritance note**: E002's only direct HLR is P1 (HLR-3), but it
   inherits P0 because the P0 reporting epic builds against its quota/
   semantics contract (an epic blocking all P0 work is implicitly P0). Flagged
   so reviewers do not read it as a priority inversion.
4. **Data-access path unspecified**: architecture context states the Dashboard
   owns no data plane and speaks the Kubernetes API only, while metering data
   is time-series usage data. The strategy does not say how reporting accesses
   it. This is folded into E001's contract validation (fields, aggregation
   rules, and access path) as cross-strategy coordination rather than a
   separate investigation — the answer is owned by the same external schema
   negotiation.
5. **"Stable API" commitment**: HLR-2's stable API for finance tooling implies
   a versioning/support commitment on the report retrieval surface; the
   implementing team should treat API stability as a deliverable property, not
   just an endpoint.
6. **Re-split trigger for E003**: the reporting epic bundles the report view,
   quota comparison, CSV export, and stable API — one logical change over one
   admin surface (splitting the view itself would build the same surface
   twice). It may exceed one sprint of effort. Re-split if implementation
   exceeds a sprint: the export/API work (HLR-2) may be split out only if a
   separately reviewable backend data-access surface emerges — never by
   splitting the admin view itself.

## Tiered Delivery

The external dependency (RHAISTRAT-9990 schema finalization) has uncertain
timing, and the strategy can deliver partial value without it:

- **Tier 1 — independent of the metering schema (start now)**:
  - E001 (risk-reduction): schema tracking and reporting-side contract
    validation can begin against RHAISTRAT-9990 drafts and concludes when the
    schema finalizes.
  - E002 (user-facing groundwork): the per-project quota reference and
    GPU-hour attribution semantics are derived from the in-platform Kueue
    quota model and do not wait on metering data.
- **Tier 2 — dependency-gated (blocked by E001 / the finalized schema)**:
  - E003: the reporting view, export, and API consume the metering data.
  - E004: documentation follows the implementations.

## Component Mapping Notes

All epic `component` values are verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`:
`Dashboard` (E001, E003), `Distributed Workloads` (E002), `Documentation`
